Subject: Pilot hosting ask + expected throughput (Sanctuary Health)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We have a 6-week pilot scoped to ingest and annotate clinician notes for two pilot hospitals. Our security and procurement teams asked for an initial recommendation: private (air-gapped/VPC) vs Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity. Key constraints:

- PHI in transit and at-rest (must be encrypted, customer-managed keys preferred)
- Need predictable p10 latency <120ms for inference on shorter prompts (~512 tokens)
- Baseline qps estimate: 30 concurrent sessions with occasional bursts to 110 qps during morning triage windows

Can you provide a recommendation, an initial GPU count estimate, and any interim mitigation (burst/fallback) we should plan for? Procurement would like a one-page matrix for their vendor evaluation.

Appreciate it,
Asha
Procurement lead, Sanctuary Health

Asha — quick acknowledgement and high-level plan below. I looped Ben and Laura to weigh in on capacity and procurement path.

Summary recommendation (short):
- For the pilot: start on Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with an explicit burst path to Hosted for peaks. This balances procurement lead time and mitigations for scale while keeping data isolation controls.

Why not Private initially:
- Private (on-prem or air-gapped) is heavier: procurement, on-site audits, and KMS integration typically add 6–10 weeks before first inference. For a 6-week pilot that kills momentum.

High-level GPU sizing rationale below — Ben and Laura please validate numbers and note any tradeoffs I missed.

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot hosting ask + expected throughput (Sanctuary Health)

Asha / team — dug into the metrics you attached and sketched a pragmatic sizing plan for the pilot and a 6–12 month posture. Notes and assumptions: 

Assumptions from CSV: average prompt 420 tokens, output 160 tokens, average latency target 120ms at p10 (inference-only), model OK to run on quantized 16-bit variants.

Pilot (weeks 1–6):
- Baseline reserved pool: 4x A400 (or equivalent 80GB-class GPUs) configured with continuous batching and KV prefix caching. Expect sustained baseline throughput ~30 qps with p10 ~90–110ms.
- Burst pathway: allow Hosted API fallback to scale extra 40–80 qps during peaks (morning triage). We model cost as Reserved + burst usage billing.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive scale-up of dedicated nodes at 75% CPU/GPU util threshold, with pre-warmed instances enabled for predictable cold-starts.

Mid-term (scale to production, 6–12 mo):
- If pilot shows 3x demand growth, move to 10x A400 equivalent pool OR shard across smaller 4x per-region pools for resiliency.

Tradeoffs:
- Dedicated gives faster onboarding than Private and better procurement predictability than Hosted-only.
- Private required for strict legal constraints (air-gapped storage of keys, ePHI custody) — if legal signs off quickly, we can run a gated Private onboarding after the pilot.

Attachments: SLARollout_v1.pdf (sample SLA ladder and fallback policy)

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Olga / Ben — quick security note from our side before procurement signs off. A few non-negotiables for any Dedicated path: 

- Customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption (we will not accept vendor-managed keys),
- Audit logs of token-level access for 90 days (searchable export),
- Ability to perform an on-site or live SOC review within 4 weeks,
- Formal data retention and deletion guarantees tied to contract terms.

If Dedicated can satisfy these, we can proceed on the pilot timetable. If not, we need to either pause and start Private onboarding or consider an interim Hosted arrangement with strict compensating controls.

-David Cho
CISO, Sanctuary Health

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

David — we can meet the asks with the Dedicated product if we include these contract and ops deliverables: 

- KMS integration: support CMK via AWS KMS or customer HSM; include standard onboarding checklist and test plan (2–3 business days for KMS config).
- Audit logs: we will provide token-level tracing and export ready for 90-day retention; sample export format attached.
- SOC review: we can schedule a live review; typical window 2–4 weeks depending on availability — for pilots we offer a scoped security briefing with redacted telemetry to accelerate sign-off.
- Data deletion: automatic purge lifecycle keyed to customer retention policy; we can add contractual SLAs for deletion within 48 hours of request except where legal hold applies.

Action items: 
1) Olga/Tessa: produce one-page matrix (Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted interim) called 1-pager_for_procurement.pdf by EOD — include cost delta band, onboarding time, required legal artifacts.
2) Ben: finalize GPU count workbook and cost model reflecting burst-to-hosted fallback.
3) Asha/David: confirm whether CMK via AWS KMS is acceptable or whether an HSM is required.

I'll assemble draft contract clauses to cover KMS and deletion guarantees.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
